doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Scope and application
summary: Applies to all federally regulated financial institutions, including foreign bank and insurance branches, on a risk basis proportional to size, strategy, risk profile, complexity and interconnectedness. Models expressly include AI and machine-learning methods.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Model risk management framework
summary: The framework sets the institution's appetite for model risk and the processes to identify, assess, manage, monitor and report it, with clear guidance for model identification, the model inventory, model risk ratings and lifecycle governance, and it covers models or data sourced externally, including from third-party vendors under Guideline B-10.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Use of models appropriate to the business purpose
summary: Models are deployed only where they meaningfully contribute to decision-making, risk assessment or a business purpose and deliver reliable outcomes consistent with their intended use.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Model identification and the enterprise model inventory
summary: The institution identifies and tracks all models in use or recently decommissioned, including vendor and third-party models, triages them for non-negligible inherent model risk, and stores those that carry it in an enterprise-level model inventory that is comprehensive, accurate, evergreen and under robust controls.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Model risk rating
summary: The institution sets a model risk rating approach that assesses the key dimensions of model risk and assigns a provisional rating to new models, updating it when the model changes materially in substance or usage.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Risk management intensity
summary: The scope, scale and intensity of model risk management is commensurate with the risk the model introduces.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Deployment in an environment with quality and change control
summary: Models are deployed into an environment with quality and change-control processes, which matters most for AI and machine-learning models that depend on several components, dynamic data sources and third-party elements.

doc: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (2027)
title: Information tracking for models
summary: For each identified model the institution maintains at least a model id, name and description, risk rating, owner, developer and origin (internally developed or vendor); for models in the inventory it also maintains version, deployment date, reviewer, approver, model dependencies, data sources and description, approved uses, limitations, last review date, monitoring status and next review date.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Technology and Cyber Risk Management
title: Technology architecture
summary: The institution implements a technology architecture framework with supporting processes so that solutions are built in line with business, technology and security requirements, and keeps that architecture comprehensive.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Technology and Cyber Risk Management
title: Technology asset management
summary: The institution maintains an updated inventory of all technology assets supporting business processes or functions, classifies them, records their configurations, provides for safe disposal and manages technology currency.

title: Disaster recovery
summary: The institution maintains an enterprise disaster recovery programme aligned with business continuity management, manages key dependencies and tests recovery scenarios.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Technology and Cyber Risk Management
title: Defend — layered preventive cyber security controls
summary: The institution designs and maintains multi-layer preventive controls: secure-by-design practices, strong cryptography and key management, enhanced controls for critical and external-facing assets, data protection and loss prevention, identity and access management and enforced configuration baselines.

title: Detect — continuous, centralised security logging
summary: The institution maintains continuous security logging for technology assets and defence layers, with central tools to aggregate, correlate and manage security event logs and enable timely access during an investigation.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-10 — Third-Party Risk Management
title: Third-party risk management framework
summary: The institution establishes an enterprise-wide framework with clear accountabilities, policies and processes covering the whole lifecycle of third-party arrangements, and reviews it regularly.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-10 — Third-Party Risk Management
title: Concentration risk
summary: Concentration risk is assessed before entering an arrangement and on an ongoing basis, across geography, supplier and subcontractor, within business units and legal entities and across the institution.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-10 — Third-Party Risk Management
title: Data security and controls, including data location
summary: The institution and the third party maintain measures to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of records and data throughout the arrangement, and set out each party's responsibilities, including where data is located.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-10 — Third-Party Risk Management
title: Contingency and exit strategy
summary: Contingency and exit plans are established in proportion to the risk and criticality of each third-party arrangement so that operations continue in normal and stressed conditions.

doc: OSFI Guideline B-10 — Third-Party Risk Management
title: Cloud-specific requirements and portability
summary: The institution develops cloud-specific requirements so that cloud adoption is planned and strategic, optimises interoperability, augments existing controls in data protection, key management and container management, and considers cloud portability.
